title: Stagger Screens for a Shooter
description: Two screeners set staggered screens one after another to free a shooter coming off a long, well-timed route to the ball.

content.objective: Use two staggered screens in sequence to fully free a shooter for a catch-and-shoot.
content.setup: A shooter starts near the baseline with two screeners set up along their path to the wing.
instructions: The shooter cuts off the first screen tight, reading the defender's path.
Immediately after, the shooter cuts off the second, staggered screen the same way.
The passer delivers the ball the instant the shooter clears the second screen.
Reset with the screeners rotating who sets the first versus the second screen.
coachingPoints: Both screens must be set and stationary in the shooter's actual path.
The shooter should brush both screens tightly, not run wide around them.
The passer needs to be ready early — the window closes fast.
commonMistakes: Screens set too far apart, giving the defender space to recover between them.
Shooter cutting wide and missing the benefit of either screen.
Standing still after a pass instead of moving with purpose.
content.safety: Screens must be legal and stationary at the moment of contact.
